dedupe_keys.name: esmi electricity supply monitoring initiative minute wise supply voltage at monitored locations across india 2014 2019 prayas energy group

description: The Electricity Supply Monitoring Initiative (ESMI) is run by Prayas (Energy Group), a non-profit organisation in Pune, India, to give evidence on the quality of electricity supply. Plug-in monitors record supply voltage every minute with an accuracy of plus or minus 4 V and send it over GPRS to a central server; the programme was launched in March 2015 and the page says it covers over 60 districts. This Harvard Dataverse deposit holds location-wise, minute-wise voltage from November 2014, with yearly or part-year files up to December 2019, a location file giving each site name, dates, district, state, rural, town or mega-city category and connection, and an about-the-initiative PDF, about 2.2 GB in total. It is free to download under CC0 1.0 and was last updated in February 2021. Coverage is monitored locations across Indian states. Caveats: a 0 reading means an outage but missing data means unavailable, not an interruption; series may not be continuous and some sites went offline; data are provided as is. Simulation uses are outage frequency, duration and voltage quality for reliability and resilience studies of Indian distribution supply. Related records: data-india-power-supply-position-daily-reports and data-india-state-daily-electricity-demand cover Indian supply at state level.
